about: The upload workbook: every tab and column. page/workbook.py reads uploads and makes the empty sheet from this file only. See the root CLAUDE.md > The upload sheet.

lines: Upload sheet: how to fill it
Organization Customers = Oracle's Create Organization Customer screen. Person Customers = Create Person Customer screen.
Order Types: one row per order type, as on Oracle's Manage Order Lookups screen. Row 4 is a sample.

Payment Terms: one row per term on Payment Terms, its installments on Payment Term Lines (in order) and its sets on Payment Term Sets. Lines and sets name their term in Payment Term Name, written exactly as the Name (capitals and spaces count).

Lookup Types: one row per NEW lookup type on Lookup Types (always a User type; type names in capitals, not starting with ORA). Its codes go on Lookup Codes, joined by Lookup Type written exactly (capitals and spaces count).

A code row whose Lookup Type is not on the Lookup Types tab adds that code to a lookup type that already exists in Oracle (User or Extensible types; System types can't get codes). Existing types and codes are never changed.
One bad code makes Oracle drop its WHOLE lookup type (the other types are saved); a rerun creates only what is missing.

Business Units: one row per business unit, as on Oracle's Create Business Unit screen (Name, Active, Location, Manager, Default Set). Order Manager and Pricing Administrator access on it for the configured user is added automatically; there is no column for it.

Business functions, ledger, legal entity, currency, profit center, service providers and set assignments are not created. An existing business unit is never changed; only missing access is added to it.

A name that differs from an existing business unit only in capitals (abd / ABD) is the same business unit for Oracle: that row is skipped and never sent. Manager: only Yaqub, Younas or Smith, Aron. Empty Location or Manager = none.

Price Lists: one row per price list (header only: no items, charges or tiers yet), as on Oracle's Create Price List screen; it is approved once its access sets are added. Price List Access Sets: one row per access set, joined by Price List Name written exactly (capitals and spaces count); every price list needs at least one.
Price list names are unique across ALL of Oracle (not per business unit), and capitals count: 'abc' next to an existing 'ABC' would be a NEW price list. An existing name is skipped and never changed.

A price list's Business Unit may also be one on the Business Units tab of this sheet: business units are created first, and the price list waits until Oracle shows that business unit for pricing. Dates: YYYY-MM-DD; Oracle shows them at 12:00 AM in the Oracle user's time zone.
Yellow headers (*) are required. Blue are optional; empty means Oracle's default.
Customers tabs: up to 100 customers per upload. A kind of setup whose tabs are empty is simply not created.
Address Purposes: one row per purpose. Customer Name = the customer's Name (organization) or First Name + space + Last Name (person).
Not in the sheet (Oracle fills them): Registry ID, Account Number, Site Number, Site on a purpose.
Dates are text, YYYY-MM-DD. Purpose dates must be within the address dates.
Test environment only. Delete the dummy rows before a real upload.

tabs.about: One row per business unit, run by the Business Units folder (2026-10-26): only the Create Business Unit screen's fields; the access (Order Manager, Pricing Administrator) is automatic. Location and Default Set drop-downs are Oracle's live lists when the sheet is made (values_live); the folder's --plan checks every value.
